context.problem_statement: Compute the 1-day Value at Risk (VaR) at 95% and 99% confidence levels for a portfolio using historical simulation. The portfolio consists of three assets with weights [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] for Asset_A, Asset_B, and Asset_C respectively. Steps: (1) compute daily portfolio returns as the weighted sum of individual asset returns, (2) sort returns in ascending order, (3) VaR at 95% = negative of the 5th percentile of returns, (4) also compute Conditional VaR (CVaR/Expected Shortfall) as the mean of returns below the VaR threshold. Report VaR and CVaR as percentage of portfolio value and in dollar terms assuming $1,000,000 portfolio.
context.expert_knowledge: Historical simulation VaR is non-parametric and captures fat tails. VaR at 95% = -percentile(returns, 5). CVaR (Expected Shortfall) = -mean(returns[returns < -VaR]). Dollar VaR = VaR_pct * portfolio_value. CVaR is a coherent risk measure while VaR is not (fails sub-additivity). Regulatory capital under Basel III uses 99% 10-day VaR.
